title: System Explorer intent declaration
description: The estate's account of what should be true, held only by hubs, hashed and compared on federation (DESIGN 08, 21). Every fact derived from it carries declared kind. Never reaches a host. Closed throughout: a typo'd member here is not noise, it is a policy that silently stops existing — protection spelled wrongly validates as an estate with nothing to protect.

reviewed.description: Review age is a fact: a declaration nobody has looked at in a year is a weaker claim (DESIGN 22). A date, not prose — the pattern stands beside the format because format is annotation-only under validators that were not asked to assert it.

estate_hub.description: The hub owning estate-scoped finding lifecycle; siblings serve those read-only (DESIGN 06, proposal).

independence.description: The failure-domain group. Two vantages on one group are redundancy; a second group is evidence (DESIGN 22).

machine_ids.description: Facts about the declared host, not its name: a changed machine-id under a declared host is a legible reinstall (DESIGN 16).

revision.description: The revision that ruled. Bounded like the document's own revision: a negative one names a ruling no revision could have made.

not_hosts.description: Classification with an author and a revision, never a filter list: an unclassified candidate is a finding until somebody rules (DESIGN 22).

instance.description: The instance the name belongs to, where a host runs more than one and they publish the same native name. Optional, and ABSENT MEANS HOST-NATIVE rather than any-instance: a denotation that matched every instance would merge them, which is acceptance item 1 arriving through the intent document instead of through a collector. A hub refuses a denotation that resolves to more than one object rather than choosing between them (DESIGN 16).

objects.description: Estate identity: the only way two hosts' native names become one object — declaration, never correlation (DESIGN 16).

plugins.description: Intent belonging to plugins this repository does not ship, keyed by plugin name (DESIGN appendix C, ruled 2026-08-20). A hub-tier plugin declares estate-wide intent exactly as a first-party concern does, and a public contract cannot enumerate one estate's concerns without making every other estate's unrepresentable — which is the subset guard wearing a schema. So this member is OPEN by construction: the shape of a stanza is the plugin's declaration to state, and this file checks only that the container is an object keyed by a plugin name whose value is an object. What that leaves unchecked is stated rather than implied: nothing here can tell a well-formed stanza from a misspelt one, and the hub asks the plugin's own declaration.

propertyNames.description: Mirrors the collector-name pattern, so a plugin may only declare intent under a name a collector could have been registered as.

additionalProperties.description: One plugin's intent, verbatim. An object rather than an array because a plugin usually has more than one kind of intent to state — protection has targets and destinations — and an array would force the first one to be the only one.

plugin_stanza_example_protection.description: NOT referenced by this schema, and deliberately. It is the shape the protection stanza had while protection was first-party, kept as the worked example of what a plugin's stanza looks like from the outside — and kept unreferenced because the moment this file validated it, the estate's concern would be back in the public contract.

destinations.description: At least one, always: a protection row with an empty destination list reads as protected and protects to nowhere — the second founding failure in a single member.
